title: Diffusion-controlled reactions with time-dependent surface reactivity
abstract: We investigate diffusion-controlled reactions on a reactive surface with time-dependent reactivity. Starting from a conventional formulation via diffusion equation with Robin boundary condition for the macroscopic concentration of particles, we aim at quantifying how temporal variations of reactivity affect the survival probability and the associated first-reaction time (FRT) of a single particle on the reactive surface. Using an adiabatic description, we first identify five long-time regimes of the first-reaction time distribution, ranging from exponential and stretched-exponential to power-law decay. In particular, sufficiently rapid decay of the reactivity leads to a nonzero probability of never reacting, despite diffusion in a bounded domain. Second, we provide a probabilistic reformulation of this problem and compare it with a different scenario of encounter-dependent reactivity. Our theoretical predictions are validated via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.
summary: This work analyzes diffusion-limited reactions on surfaces where the reaction rate changes over time. By comparing time-dependent and encounter-dependent reactivity models, the authors characterize the resulting first-reaction time statistics. The findings provide insights into how temporal variations in surface properties fundamentally alter reaction outcomes, including the possibility of permanent survival.
main_problem: The paper investigates diffusion-controlled chemical reactions occurring on a reactive surface where the surface reactivity changes over time.
main_result: The authors identify five distinct long-time regimes for the first-reaction time distribution, and show that rapid reactivity decay can lead to a non-zero probability of never reacting.
method: The study employs an adiabatic description, probabilistic reformulation, and comparison between time-dependent and encounter-dependent reactivity models.
model_or_system: The system models diffusion of particles in a bounded domain with a reactive boundary. The reaction rate is governed by a time-dependent Robin boundary condition or an encounter-dependent reactivity function.
key_observables: Survival probability, First-Reaction Time (FRT) distribution, and the total reaction rate (diffusive flux).
main_assumptions: The encounter-based approach assumes reaction attempts are independent, and the time-dependent scenario assumes reactivity modulation is controlled by intrinsic dynamics.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the paper analyzes the asymptotic behavior of the FRT distribution across different decay regimes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the standard constant reactivity model to the advanced cases of time-dependent reactivity $\kappa(t)$ and encounter-dependent reactivity $\kappa_e(\ell)$, comparing theoretical predictions with Monte Carlo simulations.
why_interesting: The analysis of non-equilibrium dynamics, first passage times, and the transition between different decay regimes (exponential to power-law) is highly relevant to open quantum systems and reaction dynamics.
